meaning: Holy shit! / WTF! / No way!
note: The most versatile exclamation in modern informal Chinese. Can express shock, anger, admiration, or disbelief depending on tone.
example_hz: 卧槽，这也太酷了吧！
example_py: Wòcáo, zhè yě tài kù le ba!
example_en: Holy shit, this is way too cool!

meaning: Badass / awesome / insane skill
note: Universal praise for someone who does something extraordinarily well or impressive.
example_hz: 哥们儿，你这也太牛逼了！
example_py: Gēmenr, nǐ zhè yě tài niúbī le!
example_en: Bro, you are seriously freaking awesome!

meaning: What the hell? / What are you doing?
note: Expresses annoyance when someone does something confusing, slow, or frustrating.
example_hz: 搞毛啊，怎么还没来？
example_py: Gǎo máo a, zěnme hái méi lái?
example_en: What the hell, why haven't they arrived yet?

meaning: No way / Not a chance! / Forget about it
note: Direct, informal way to reject an impossible or ridiculous request.
example_hz: 借钱给你？没门儿！
example_py: Jiè qián gěi nǐ? Méiménr!
example_en: Lend you money? Not a chance!

meaning: Reliable / trustworthy / solid
note: Extremely common in daily life and business. Opposite is 不靠谱 (shady / flaky).
example_hz: 找他帮忙肯定没问题，这人办事很靠谱。
example_py: Zhǎo tā bāngmáng kěndìng méi wèntí, zhè rén bànshì hěn kàopǔ.
example_en: Asking him for help won't be a problem, he is very reliable.

meaning: Speechless / rolling my eyes
note: When something is so absurd, stupid, or ridiculous that you have no words to describe it.
example_hz: 看了这个新闻，我真是一整个无语。
example_py: Kàn le zhège xīnwén, wǒ zhēn shì yī zhěng gè wúyǔ.
example_en: After seeing this news, I am honestly completely speechless.

meaning: To vent / roast / complain / air grievances
note: Originally from Japanese manzai comedy (tsukkomi), now ubiquitous in Chinese for witty complaining or roasting.
example_hz: 我想吐槽一下昨天的电影，真的太难看了。
example_py: Wǒ xiǎng tùcáo yīxià zuótiān de diànyǐng, zhēn de tài nánkàn le.
example_en: I need to vent about yesterday's movie, it was truly horrible.

meaning: To scroll on phone / doomscroll
note: 刷 literally means to brush/swipe. Describes endlessly flicking through TikTok, Xiaohongshu, or social media.
example_hz: 别整天在床上刷手机了，出去晒晒太阳。
example_py: Bié zhěngtiān zài chuáng shang shuā shǒujī le, chūqù shàishài tàiyáng.
example_en: Stop doomscrolling in bed all day, go outside and get some sun.

meaning: To give a 'like' / thumbs up
note: Used on all Chinese social apps, and also figuratively in speech for 'giving props' to someone.
example_hz: 要是觉得有用，别忘了点个赞！
example_py: Yàoshi juéde yǒuyòng, bié wàng le diǎn gè zàn!
example_en: If you found this helpful, don't forget to leave a like!

meaning: WeChat (the app for everything in China)
note: China's operating system for daily life: messaging, payments, restaurant ordering, taxis.
example_hz: 加个微信吧，回头发定位给你。
example_py: Jiā gè wēixìn ba, huítóu fā dìngwèi gěi nǐ.
example_en: Let's add WeChat, I'll send you the location pin later.

meaning: Food delivery / takeout
note: Ordering via Meituan or Ele.me is a cornerstone of daily life in China.
example_hz: 今晚太累不想做饭，叫外卖吧。
example_py: Jīnwǎn tài lèi bù xiǎng zuòfàn, jiào wàimài ba.
example_en: Too tired to cook tonight, let's just order delivery.

meaning: To hail a taxi / order a ride (Didi)
note: 打 (dǎ) is used idiomatically for calling/hailing transport.
example_hz: 外面雨下得太大了，我们打车走吧。
example_py: Wàimiàn yǔ xià de tài dà le, wǒmen dǎchē zǒu ba.
example_en: The rain outside is pouring, let's call a taxi.

meaning: Check please! / To pay the bill
note: What you yell to the restaurant staff when ready to pay.
example_hz: 服务员，买单！打包这两个菜。
example_py: Fúwùyuán, mǎidān! Dǎbāo zhè liǎng gè cài.
example_en: Waiter, bill please! And pack up these two dishes.

meaning: Whatever / Up to you / Anything is fine
note: The most common response in Chinese when asked what to eat or do. Can be neutral or dismissive depending on tone.
example_hz: 中午去哪儿吃？——随便，我都行。
example_py: Zhōngwǔ qù nǎr chī? —— Suíbiàn, wǒ dōu xíng.
example_en: Where to eat for lunch? —— Whatever, anything works for me.

meaning: Forget it / Drop it / Let it go
note: Used to concede, stop an argument, or give up on an idea.
example_hz: 算了吧，别再跟他争了，没意思。
example_py: Suànle ba, bié zài gēn tā zhēng le, méi yìsi.
example_en: Forget it, don't argue with him anymore, it's pointless.

meaning: What are you doing? / Why? / What for?
note: Informal contraction of 干什么. Can sound playful, defensive, or curious.
example_hz: 你干嘛这样看着我？我脸上有东西吗？
example_py: Nǐ gànmá zhèyàng kàn zhe wǒ? Wǒ liǎn shang yǒu dōngxi ma?
example_en: Why are you looking at me like that? Is there something on my face?

meaning: Really?! / Are you serious?! / For real?
note: Everyday conversational exclamation when hearing surprising gossip or news.
example_hz: 真的假的？他居然把老板给炒了？
example_py: Zhēn de jiǎ de? Tā jīurán bǎ lǎobǎn gěi chǎo le?
example_en: For real?! He actually fired his boss?!

meaning: Awkward / cringey / embarrassing
note: Describes social awkwardness, second-hand embarrassment, or uncomfortable situations.
example_hz: 刚才打招呼认错人了，场面极度尴尬。
example_py: Gāngcái dǎ zhāohu rèncuò rén le, chǎngmiàn jídù gāngà.
example_en: I just waved at the wrong person, the situation was insanely awkward.

meaning: Excuse me / Sorry / Feeling embarrassed
note: Lighter than 对不起 (I'm sorry). Used when bumping into someone, asking a favor, or feeling grateful/shy.
example_hz: 不好意思借过一下，我赶时间。
example_py: Bù hǎoyìsi jièguò yīxià, wǒ gǎn shíjiān.
example_en: Excuse me, coming through, I'm in a rush.

meaning: Almost / roughly / more or less / close enough
note: Famous cultural concept in Chinese life: things don't need to be 100% exact, 'close enough' is fine.
example_hz: 时间差不多了，我们准备出发吧。
example_py: Shíjiān chàbuduō le, wǒmen zhǔnbèi chūfā ba.
example_en: Time is pretty much up, let's get ready to head out.

meaning: To work for a boss / wage labor
note: Origin of the viral meme '打工人' (working-class laborer striving every day).
example_hz: 加油打工人！今天又是元气满满的一天。
example_py: Jiāyóu dǎgōngrén! Jīntiān yòu shì yuánqì mǎnmǎn de yī tiān.
example_en: Keep pushing, wage worker! Another day full of energy.

meaning: Lying flat / opting out of the rat race
note: Major youth culture term for rejecting extreme hustle culture and doing the bare minimum.
example_hz: 这周工作太累了，周末我只想躺平不看任何消息。
example_py: Zhè zhōu gōngzuò tài lèi le, zhōumò wǒ zhǐ xiǎng tǎngpíng bù kàn rènhé xiāoxi.
example_en: Work was too tiring this week, on the weekend I just want to lie flat and ignore all messages.

meaning: Hyper-competitive rat race / involution
note: When competition becomes so fierce that everyone works harder just to stay in the same place.
example_hz: 现在的行业内卷太严重了，大家天天加班。
example_py: Xiànzài de hángyè nèijuǎn tài yánzhòng le, dàjiā tiāntiān jiābān.
example_en: The rat race in this industry is too intense now, everyone works overtime every day.

meaning: Tired as a dog / dog-tired / exhausted
note: Vivid Chinese idiom used when completely worn out after a long day.
example_hz: 搬了一整天家，现在真是累成狗了。
example_py: Bān le yī zhěng tiān jiā, xiànzài zhēn shì lèi chéng gǒu le.
example_en: Moved houses all day long, right now I am honestly tired as a dog.

meaning: Cup / glass / mug
note: Basic household object missing from the original deck.
example_hz: 请帮我倒一杯水，杯子在桌子上。
example_py: Qǐng bāng wǒ dào yī bēi shuǐ, bēizi zài zhuōzi shang.
example_en: Please help me pour a glass of water, the cup is on the table.

meaning: Instant noodles / ramen
note: 泡面 (pàomiàn) is the colloquial term for noodles brewed with boiling water.
example_hz: 大半夜饿了，煮一碗方便面加个蛋最舒服。
example_py: Dà bànyè è le, zhǔ yī wǎn fāngbiànmiàn jiā gè dàn zuì shūfu.
example_en: Hungry in the middle of the night, cooking a bowl of instant noodles with an egg hits the spot.

meaning: Tomato
note: 北方 (North China) commonly says 西红柿, while 南方 (South) often says 番茄.
example_hz: 西红柿炒鸡蛋是每个中国人都会做的家常菜。
example_py: Xīhóngshì chǎo jīdàn shì měi gè zhōngguórén dōu huì zuò de jiāchángcài.
example_en: Tomato scrambled eggs is a home-style dish that every Chinese person knows how to make.

meaning: Banana
note: Common fruit missing from the original sentence deck.
example_hz: 去超市买一把香蕉和几个苹果。
example_py: Qù chāoshì mǎi yī bǎ xiāngjiāo hé jǐ gè píngguǒ.
example_en: Go to the supermarket to buy a bunch of bananas and a few apples.

meaning: To see a doctor / to seek medical care
note: Used both for the patient 'seeing a doctor' and the doctor 'treating patients'.
example_hz: 他发烧两天了，今天必须去医院看病。
example_py: Tā fāshāo liǎng tiān le, jīntiān bìxū qù yīyuàn kànbìng.
example_en: He's had a fever for two days, he must go to the hospital to see a doctor today.

meaning: To have a holiday / to have days off
note: Notice the 4th tone on 假 (jià = holiday, distinct from jiǎ = fake).
example_hz: 下周我们放假三天，你有什么打算？
example_py: Xià zhōu wǒmen fàngjià sān tiān, nǐ yǒu shénme dǎsuàn?
example_en: We have three days off next week, do you have any plans?

meaning: To work overtime
note: Unavoidable topic in Chinese professional life.
example_hz: 今天又要加班，可能赶不上最后一班地铁了。
example_py: Jīntiān yòu yào jiābān, kěnéng gǎnbushàng zuìhòu yī bān dìtiě le.
example_en: Working overtime again today, might not catch the last subway train.
